correction.text: Kong and the Senufo country of north-eastern Ivory Coast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kong row). Seku Watara seized Kong c. 1710 and expanded along the trade routes. The page gives no area: "northeastern present-day Ivory Coast and much of Burkina Faso, plus parts of Mali and Ghana" at its greatest extent (undated, so only the core is drawn).

union.text: Kong and the Senufo country of north-eastern Ivory Coast
Sya (Bobo-Dioulasso), reached in 1737 and left to Seku's son

keyframe_review.note: "Seku eventually reached Sya in 1737" (Bobo-Dioulasso) and reached the Black Volta region; Famagan's 1739-40 western campaign took Sofara and besieged Ségou for nine months before a Fula column relieved it, with no lasting hold. Gyaman stayed under Ashanti control in a stalemate with Kong. Kénédougou is a vassal 1737-1825 (not in the shape). [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: the shape now runs 1737-1739; Gwiriko takes the area around Bobo-Dioulasso in 1740 (Gwiriko page), see kong-empire_1740.]

correction.text: Kong and the Senufo country of north-eastern Ivory Coast, without Sya: the Sya disc goes to Gwiriko in 1740

keyframe_review.note: Gwiriko page: Famagan "refused to pay allegiance to Sekou Ouattara's sons and seized the area which included Tiefo, Dafin, and Bwamu" (infobox: independence from Kong Empire 1740); its capital is Bobo-Dioulasso. The Kong page has Seku die "around 1745", split the empire into "mostly separate fiefdoms ruled by Watara family members" and does not name Gwiriko. Gwiriko's provinces (Houet, Tuy, Mou Houn) cover about two thirds of the old 100 km Sya disc (20,991 km2); the rest of the disc has no later hold on any page and is dropped with it. The Kong page's wider extent ("much of present-day Burkina Faso and parts of Mali and Ghana": the Black Volta, Gonja and Dagomba, limited control of the Lobi gold trade in 1840) is undated or outline-less and is not drawn. No area figure on any page.

region.text: Kong and the Senufo country of north-eastern Ivory Coast

ledger.note: c. 1710: Seku Watara founds the Kong Empire. Infobox "Established: 1710, founding of Kong dynasty by Seku Watara"; he "deposed and killed an important leader in Kong, Lasiri Gbambele", uniting the Dyula leaders.

region.text: Sya (Bobo-Dioulasso), reached in 1737 and left to Seku's son

ledger.note: 1737: Seku Watara reaches Sya (Bobo-Dioulasso). "Seku eventually reached Sya in 1737, where he left one of his sons in charge before returning to Kong."

region.text: Kénédougou, whose independence from Kong dates from 1825

ledger.note: Kénédougou is Kong's dependency from the rise of Kong; the Kénédougou page gives only its end (independence 1825) and lists the Kong Empire as predecessor, so 1737 is a bridging year (confidence 1). Kénédougou page (re-read 2026-10-19): "In the 18th century, Kénédougou was a far-flung extension of the Kong Empire"; the Kong page (re-read) does not mention the dependency; 1737 stays a bridge inside the century and Kong's rise (1710).

region.text: Sya (Bobo-Dioulasso), reached in 1737 and left to Seku's son

ledger.note: About 1740: Gwiriko breaks away and takes the Bobo-Dioulasso area. Gwiriko page: Famagan "refused to pay allegiance to Sekou Ouattara's sons and seized the area which included Tiefo, Dafin, and Bwamu" (infobox "Established independence from Kong Empire: 1740"). The year is the page's; applying it to the whole Sya disc is a reading (the Kong page, re-read 2026-10-19, has Seku die "around 1745" and does not name Gwiriko). Matches gwiriko /ledger/1 (gain 1740 cp kong-empire). [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: was missing; Kong kept the disc to 1897 and double-claimed about 21,000 km2 with Gwiriko.]

region.text: Kénédougou, whose independence from Kong dates from 1825

ledger.note: 1825: Kénédougou becomes independent of Kong. Infobox "Independence from Kong Empire: 1825"; under Doaula Ba Traoré the kingdom "was able to establish independence" as Kong power declined.

region.text: Kong and the Senufo country of north-eastern Ivory Coast

ledger.note: May 1897: Samori destroys Kong. The Kong page: "Samory destroyed the city, either on May 23, 1897, or on May 18, 1898" and gives 1898 in the infobox; the Wassoulou Empire page has Samori destroy Kong on 23 May 1897 after a revolt (followed).

wars.name: Kong-Ashanti conflict over Gyaman
wars.outcome: "Conflict broke out between Kong and another growing power", the Ashanti Empire, in the mid-18th century: "a stalemate, with Ashanti in control of Gyaaman but recognizing Kong's independence."
wars.note: The page dates it only to "the mid-1700s"; 1740-1780 is a span.

wars.name: Famagan's western campaign and the siege of Ségou
wars.outcome: In November 1739 Seku's brother Famagan "launched a major military operation westwards": Sofara taken, Ségou besieged for nine months until a Fula relief column broke the siege.

wars.outcome: Monteil's French column, sent in August 1894, was forced to retreat after fighting on the 14th; Kong pledged fealty to Samori in April 1895 and Samori destroyed the city in 1897.

notes:
Kong Empire (Wattara Empire), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Kong Empire, Kénédougou Kingdom, Wassoulou Empire.

Ends 1897 (May 23: Wassoulou and Samori pages, and the Wassoulou dossier's vassal_end); the Kong infobox says dissolved 1898 and offers "May 23, 1897" or "May 18, 1898" for the burning. The Kong page does not mention conquests of Kénédougou, Gonja, Gyaman, Jimini or Bouna (the group scope's list), a km2 area, a rulers list, or the French conquest; Kénédougou's 1825 independence comes from the Kénédougou page, the earlier vassalage is a bridge. The shape is the core plus Sya; the "much of Burkina Faso" extent is not drawn. The Kong page mentions Karamokho Oule dominating the second half of the 19th century without being king.
Counterparts: senufo-chiefdoms (predecessor, no dossier), kenedougou-kingdom (this batch), ashanti-empire (exists), bamana-empire (exists). Gazetteer: Kong (place), Sya (alias of Bobo Dioulasso), Sofara.

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail): (a) New loss 1740 cp gwiriko (c2) with the Sya disc and a keyframe kong-empire_1740 (1740-1897) without it, so Kong and Gwiriko no longer double-claim about 21,000 km2 for 1740-1897. The remaining third of the old disc (about 10,000 km2, outside Houet, Tuy and Mou Houn) is dropped with it because no page ties it to Kong after 1740. The Kong page puts Seku's death 'around 1745', five years after Gwiriko's 1740 independence (Gwiriko page): the dates are not reconciled; the Gwiriko page's year is used. (b) The Kong page's extent ('much of present-day Burkina Faso and parts of Mali and Ghana') stays undrawn: the page, re-read, gives only the Black Volta (undated), Gonja and Dagomba (conflicts, undated) and 1840 limited control of the Lobi gold trade; no outline, so a gap. (c) The Wassoulou dossier now carries the matching gain 1897/5 cp kong-empire (Savanes), closing the cross-check on the dissolve. (d) Kénédougou's dependency stays a c1 bridge at 1737: the Kénédougou page says only 'in the 18th century' it was an extension of Kong.
